prompt: A single wide conceptual painting places a self-standing, featureless humanoid machine at the center, its many arms simultaneously translating text, moving chess pieces, studying an unfamiliar textbook, and transferring glowing skill-lines from one domain to another while no human operator is present; to its left sit a simple calculator and a chess engine, clearly limited to one job each. A blurred, unlabeled threshold with a giant question mark cuts across the scene, marking the absence of any agreed test. On the right an executive holds a chart of the machine outperforming humans at most paid work, while clustered researchers gesture toward the same figure as both half-realized in today’s large models and still wrapped in science-fiction tropes. Far behind and vastly larger looms a superintelligent form that dwarfs every human-scale task. In the foreground a philosopher, a lawmaker and a company founder overlap as they utter the same two words, and an open statute lies between them whose undefined terms leave builders without any clear prohibition.
